title: Semiconductor Devices and Models
intro: Diodes and transistors are written as an instance line that names a model, and a .model line that holds the model's parameters. ngspice has built-in models from the 1970s Shichman-Hodges MOSFET to BSIM4, BSIM-SOI, HiSIM and a power-MOS VDMOS model, and loads every modern Verilog-A model (BSIM-CMG, PSP, Mextram, HICUM) through OSDI.

blocks.source:
* Dname n+ n- model [area] [m=] [pj=] [off] [ic=] [temp=] [dtemp=]
D1   a  k  dmod
* Qname nc nb ne [ns] [tj] model [area] [areac=] [areab=] [m=] [off] [ic=vbe,vce] [temp=]
Q1   c  b  e  npn1
* Jname nd ng ns model [area] [m=] [off] [ic=] [temp=]
J1   d  g  s  njf
* Zname nd ng ns model [area] [m=] [off]      (MESFET, HFET)
* Mname nd ng ns nb model [L=] [W=] [AD=] [AS=] [PD=] [PS=] [NRD=] [NRS=] [m=] [nf=] [off] [ic=]
M1   d  g  s  b  nch L=0.18u W=2u AD=1p AS=1p PD=5u PS=5u m=4
.model dmod  D    (is=1e-14 n=1.05 rs=0.5 cjo=2p vj=0.7 m=0.5 tt=5n bv=50 ibv=10u)
.model npn1  NPN  (is=1e-16 bf=150 vaf=80 rb=100 rc=20 re=1 cje=1p cjc=0.5p tf=20p)
.model njf   NJF  (vto=-2 beta=1e-3 lambda=0.01)
.model nch   NMOS (level=14 version=4.8.3 tox=4n vth0=0.45)

blocks.text: The model type is the second word of .model: D, NPN, PNP, NJF, PJF, NMOS, PMOS, NMF, PMF (MESFET), VDMOS, and for OSDI models the Verilog-A module name. area (or m) scales a device: area = 4 is four unit devices in parallel. off starts the device off in the operating-point search, a convergence aid for circuits with two stable states.

The diode model is the SPICE junction diode: saturation current IS with emission coefficient N, series resistance RS, depletion capacitance CJO, VJ, M (plus sidewall CJSW, VJSW, MJSW with the perimeter pj), transit time TT, breakdown BV and IBV, high-injection knee IKF, recombination ISR and NR, and temperature parameters EG, XTI. Version 46 updated the sidewall diode and added a soft-recovery model with an internal charge node for power diodes. level=3 gives geometry from W and L of the instance.

blocks.source:
Diode I-V and its small-signal resistance
.model d1n4148 D (is=2.52n rs=0.568 n=1.752 cjo=4p m=0.4 tt=20n bv=100 ibv=100u)
V1 a 0 DC 0
D1 a 0 d1n4148
.control
  dc V1 0.3 0.8 0.01
  let id = -i(V1)
  meas dc vf1m find v(a) when id=1m
  alter V1 0.65
  op
  show D1 : id gd
.endc
.end

blocks.text: show prints the operating-point quantities of a device; showmod prints its model parameters. Every device has its own list (id, gd, cd for a diode; ic, ib, gm, gpi, cpi for a BJT; id, vth, gm, gds, gmbs, cgg, vdsat for a BSIM MOSFET), shown by devhelp D, devhelp Q and so on.

items: level=1 (default): the Gummel-Poon model, with optional quasi-saturation (RCO, VO, GAMMA, QCO) and lateral-PNP substrate options. Four-terminal form with a substrate node.
level=4: VBIC, with an optional fifth thermal node for self-heating (version 45 revised it).
Mextram and HICUM/L0, and newer VBIC releases, come as Verilog-A through OSDI.

blocks.source:
BJT output characteristics: a nested DC sweep
.model qn NPN (is=1e-16 bf=200 vaf=60 br=2 rb=50 rc=10 cje=1p cjc=0.4p tf=30p)
Vce c 0 DC 0
Ib  0 b DC 10u
Q1  c b 0 qn
.control
  dc Vce 0 5 0.05 Ib 5u 25u 5u      $ inner Vce, outer Ib
  let ic = -i(Vce)
  meas dc ic_at_3v find ic at=3
  alter Vce 3
  op
  show Q1 : ic gm gpi
.endc
.end

blocks.text: In a nested DC sweep all outer steps go into one plot as one long vector; the meas above finds the first crossing of 3 V, which is the 5 uA curve. To pull out each curve, loop in the control language instead (Sweeps, Corners and Monte Carlo page).

JFET level 1 is the Shichman-Hodges model with the Parker-Skellern modification, level 2 the full Parker-Skellern model. MESFETs (Z elements) use the Statz model (level 1), with level 2 and 3 for the Ytterdal and Lee HFET models and level 5 and 6 for HFET1 and HFET2.

items: level 1 (Shichman-Hodges), 2 (Grove-Frohman), 3 (semi-empirical), 6 and 9: hand-analysis and teaching models; level 1 has KP, VTO, LAMBDA, GAMMA, PHI and the Meyer capacitances.
level 4 and 5: BSIM1 and BSIM2, historical.
level 8 or 49: BSIM3, with versions 3.0, 3.1, 3.2 to 3.2.4 and 3.3.0 selected by version=.
level 14 or 54: BSIM4, versions 4.0 to 4.5, 4.6.2, 4.7.0 and 4.8.3 (default the newest). This is the model of most 180 nm to 28 nm planar PDKs, including SkyWater SKY130 and GF180MCU.
level 10 or 58: BSIM-SOI (B4SOI 4.3.1); 55, 56, 57 for the older fully-, dynamically- and partially-depleted BSIM3SOI; 60 the Southampton STAG SOI model.
level 68: HiSIM2 (2.8.0); level 73: HiSIM_HV for LDMOS.

VDMOS: a power-MOSFET model (with weak inversion, quasi-saturation, self-heating and a body diode with soft recovery) that reads the .model lines of discrete MOSFETs as LTspice uses them: .model irf540 VDMOS(...).
Through OSDI: BSIM-BULK, BSIM-CMG (FinFET and gate-all-around), BSIM-IMG, PSP 103 (used by IHP SG13G2), HiSIM variants, and others.

blocks.source:
NMOS characteristics with BSIM4 default parameters
M1 d g 0 0 nch L=0.18u W=1u
.model nch NMOS (level=14 version=4.8.3)
Vd d 0 DC 1.8
Vg g 0 DC 0
.control
  dc Vg 0 1.8 0.01
  let id = -i(Vd)
  let gm = deriv(id)
  meas dc gm_max max gm
  meas dc vt_lin find v(g) when id=1u      $ constant-current threshold
  alter Vg 1.0
  op
  print @m1[gm] @m1[gds] @m1[vth] @m1[vdsat] @m1[cgg]
.endc
.end

blocks.text: @device[parameter] reads a device's internal value. In a sweep, save it first: save @m1[gm] before the dc command, because by default only node voltages and source currents are kept. In AC analysis @-values are not available; use the operating point.

PDK models are often split into bins of length and width: nch.1, nch.2, ... each with lmin, lmax, wmin and wmax. The instance names the base name (nch) and ngspice picks the bin that contains its L and W. This works for BSIM3 and BSIM4. A device outside every bin gives an error saying no model was found for that L and W: check units (W=1 is one metre) and the scale option.

blocks.source:
Binned model
.model nch.1 NMOS (level=14 lmin=0.15u lmax=1u   wmin=0.4u wmax=100u vth0=0.45)
.model nch.2 NMOS (level=14 lmin=1u    lmax=100u wmin=0.4u wmax=100u vth0=0.40)
M1 d g 0 0 nch L=0.5u W=2u
M2 e g 0 0 nch L=5u   W=2u
Vd d 0 1
Ve e 0 1
Vg g 0 0.8
.control
  op
  print @m1[vth] @m2[vth]
.endc
.end

items: L and W are the drawn sizes; the model's dl/dw (or lint/wint) make the effective ones. .option scale=1e-6 lets you write L=0.18 for 0.18 um; PDKs often rely on it, so copy their options.
AD, AS, PD, PS (drain and source diffusion areas and perimeters) set the junction capacitances. Leaving them out leaves those capacitances out, which makes circuits look faster than they are.

nf (BSIM4): number of fingers; m: parallel devices; sa, sb, sd: stress-effect distances; delvto and mulu0 (BSIM4 instance parameters) shift threshold and mobility for one device, the usual way to apply mismatch.
off and ic=vds,vgs,vbs: convergence aid and transient initial condition.

blocks.text: Every model is evaluated at the circuit temperature (.temp or .options temp=, default 27 C) relative to its tnom (default 27 C). temp= and dtemp= on an instance set one device's temperature, a simple way to model self-heating or a hot spot. Safe-operating-area limits (bv_max, vgs_max, ..., set in the model) print warnings when exceeded once you set .option warn=1 (maxwarns limits how many); the --soa-log option writes them to a file.

blocks.title: Which level
blocks.text: A model file starts with .model nfet NMOS (level=54 version=4.5 ...). Which ngspice model will evaluate it, and what happens with level=49?
solution: level=54 is BSIM4 (same as 14), and version=4.5 selects the 4.0-to-4.5 code.
level=49 is BSIM3 (same as 8); version picks 3.0, 3.1, 3.2.x or 3.3.0.

blocks.title: Missing capacitance
blocks.text: A ring oscillator of BSIM4 inverters runs 30% faster in simulation than measured. Name two netlist omissions that do this.
solution: AD, AS, PD, PS left out: no drain and source junction capacitance.
No parasitic wiring capacitance (no extracted netlist), or nf and sa/sb not given so layout effects are missing. Also check .option scale if sizes were written without units.
blocks.answer: Missing AD/AS/PD/PS and missing wiring parasitics.

items: H. Vogt, G. Atkinson, D. Warning and P. Nenzi, Ngspice User's Manual, version 47, 2026 (ngspice.sourceforge.io/docs.html), chapter 7 (diodes, BJTs, JFETs, MESFETs, MOSFETs) and chapter 27 (device parameters).
BSIM4 Manual, BSIM Group, University of California, Berkeley (bsim.berkeley.edu).
P. Antognetti and G. Massobrio, Semiconductor Device Modeling with SPICE, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill, 1993.
